verdicts.reason: All quotes verbatim. 04.01.01:101 taxonomy row for `Member wanted` reads 'Derived — the event date'; 04.01.01:321 D-16 names 'member wanted' explicitly in its presence-type list deriving from 'the event date', states 'It is never absent', and 04.01.01:110-111 states 'no type can publish without a decide-by'. Against that, 04.06:36 'Lifecycle | Deadline-bound | **Open-ended; runs for months**' and 04.06:63 'Open | Ad posted | Live, open-ended, no deadline'. A third reading exists at 04.02.01:60 ('Poster closes it, or 90 days elapse') and 04.02.01:280 Q-06 itself reads the member-wanted decide-by as 'a 90-day recency curve' — while 04.02.01:255 D-06 says the board tombstone is 'presentation only' and 'never closes the post'. Grepped the whole domain for any definition of a member-wanted post's date: none exists (only 04.01.01:101 and D-16 mention it, both circularly). No reconciliation in opportunities-casting-index.md or opportunities-casting-cx.md (grep for 'decide-by' returns zero hits in both). 04.06 is [SURFACE], last updated 2026-07-16; D-16 was ratified 2026-07-30 without touching it. Two normative statements ('always present, no type can publish without one' vs 'open-ended, no deadline') cannot both hold, and the derivation base is undefined for a type that has no event.

Quotes verbatim: 04.01.01:96 and :98 both read 'Asked — a real field, pre-filled with the deadline', :98 citing '(04.07 D-05)'; 04.01.01:109-111 'Both still default to the deadline if left alone, which is why no type can publish without a decide-by either way'; 04.07:105 D-05 'not derived from the deadline … Deriving it would tell 2,000 acts they will hear by 1 March, which is the ghosting D-04 exists to prevent, generated by the platform rather than the Operator'; 04.07:44 'a decide-by the Operator states'. DOWNGRADED from blocking: the claim overstates by framing 04.01.01 as saying the field is derived — it says 'Asked … pre-filled', and a pre-fill is not a derivation, so the two headline labels agree (both files cross-cite each other approvingly). The live residue is narrower but real and normative on both sides: 04.01.01:110 permits publishing with an untouched deadline-valued decide-by, which is precisely the platform-generated date 04.07 D-05 calls the ghosting harm. 04.07 D-05 nowhere states the field must be blocking-required-with-no-default, so this is a genuine unresolved divergence rather than an impasse — warning, not blocking.

Quotes are accurate (04.01.01:47 'Soft ceiling: **25 slots per post**', :313 D-08 'Soft ceiling 25 slots', :185 'Refused above 25; routed to the open call shape (04.07)'), but the divergence does not survive. The two 'soft ceiling' mentions state a threshold and never state a behaviour at 26; the single place the file states behaviour — the Edge Cases row at :185 — states refusal AND its user-facing string ('That's a hiring round, not an opportunity — open calls handle 30 slots properly.'). The finding's own argument cuts the other way: because this file has explicit warn-not-block vocabulary (:196, :318 D-13) and deliberately did NOT use it here, and instead wrote 'Refused', the behaviour is stated once and unambiguously. 'Soft' is doing tunability work (like D-13's 'tunable at /create-prd' intervals), not warn-vs-block work. Two competent implementers reading the file whole converge on block-and-route.

The freshness rule at :62-64 has the same hole ('48 h for dep/session/function/crew/support, 30 days for member-wanted, never for deadline-bearing types'). Grepped the whole domain: 'Open-mic' appears only in 04.01.01 and 04.01.03 (compensation), 'General call' only in 04.01.01 and the 04.01 index — neither appears anywhere in 04.02. No default/fallback rule exists for unlisted types, and 04.02.01:254 D-05 makes the scoping normative ('Board decay, sort and tombstone windows are type-scoped'). General call is genuinely underdetermined because its date semantics are poster-chosen, so it cannot even be sorted into the freshness rule's deadline-bearing / not-deadline-bearing split. Not a tracked deferral — no marker, no owner, no target.

Quotes are accurate (04.06:56 orphaned marker; 04.06:103 'which has run'; 04.04.01:228 and 04.05.01:259 Q-05 scoped to the debt), but the forced invention does not survive. The post's own behaviour is determined by defaults: 04.01.01:321 D-16 makes the decide-by what closes the post, :313 D-08 makes post status follow its slots and 'never set directly', and :246 enumerates Withdrawn's triggers — nothing dissolves a post, so it stays live to its decide-by. The dissolution case itself is also covered at 04.04.01:142, 04.04.03:176 and 04.05.01:165 with tracked Q-05s. Quotes accurate (04.03.03:102 D-03, :59, :76, :111 Q-03 RESOLVED; 04.03-cx:152-153 carries exactly the quoted sentence — the finding cites :153, the sentence wraps 152-153, which is not a misquote). CX-05's trigger chain reads 'Evidence resolved → threshold met', and the evidence model it names is the explicit ordered ladder at 04.03.02:38-46 — five named evidence types 'in descending order of strength', with the strongest ('Verified credit with attestor') and weakest ('Self-claimed skills') fixed. Two competent implementers converge on 'poster picks a minimum evidence tier'.
